title: Advanced test callbacks remain bounded without general closures
observed_need: Declare named tests, suites, fixtures, parameterized cases, and test metadata without a parallel host registry.
current_language_behavior: Profile 0.17 has a first-class test declaration and the compiler emits a static inventory; unrestricted first-class handler/closure values remain unavailable for dynamic fixtures, middleware, and callback-driven parameterization.
why_insufficient: Normal test discovery no longer requires manifest names or a handwritten suite, but advanced fixture/callback composition cannot yet be expressed as bounded callable values.
minimal_reproducer: tests/self_suite.mncs uses six source test declarations and no suite registry; a dynamic fixture callback still has no native callable-value representation.
desired_direction: A native test declaration/metadata vocabulary and first-class callable/fixture abstraction that remains bounded, typed, and statically inspectable.
workaround: Compiler inventory supplies static declarations; native assertion/property/snapshot modules remain explicit and advanced callback features stay constrained rather than synthesized through a host registry.
